narrative.title: Field Parser on a Noisy Boot Bus
narrative.scenario: An embedded controller reads configuration tokens off a serial bus where sensor firmware appends free-form annotations around the numeric fields. The parser must behave like the C library: skip leading blanks, honour one sign character, consume the digit run, ignore everything after it, and saturate at the 32-bit register bounds instead of wrapping. A field that never reaches a digit yields zero.
narrative.inputFormat: A string s that may contain leading spaces, an optional '+' or '-' sign, digits, and arbitrary trailing characters.
narrative.outputFormat: The parsed 32-bit signed integer: digits read with their sign, clamped to [-2^31, 2^31 - 1] on overflow, or 0 when no digits are read.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, the space ' ', and the characters '+', '-', '.'

testCases.explanation: No blanks, no sign — the digit run is read straight through.
The leading blank is skipped and the '-' fixes the sign before the digits are consumed.

hintLevels: Level 1: Four phases in strict order — blanks, one optional sign, the digit run, then stop reading entirely.
Level 2: Accumulate into a wider container than the answer type so overflow is detected as it happens, not after the value wraps.
Level 3: Clamp direction matters: a positive run past the cap returns 2^31 - 1 while a negative one returns -2^31 — and a sign not followed by digits means 0.
